name: Free TAFE (Fee-Free TAFE)
provider: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations
summary: Free TAFE and VET course places funded nationally and delivered by each state and territory, prioritised for groups who face barriers to study.
key: At least 100,000 Free TAFE and VET places per year from 2027, now a permanent feature of the national VET system.
who: Places are prioritised for First Nations Australians, young people aged 17 to 24, people out of work or receiving income support, unpaid carers, women facing economic insecurity, women studying in non-traditional fields, people with disability and certain visa holders.
Eligibility details may vary by state and territory.
how: Check course eligibility on the Your Career Free TAFE page, then enrol through a TAFE or provider in your state or territory.
catches: Free TAFE is delivered in partnership with states and territories, so the courses on offer and the exact rules depend on where you live.

evidence.claim: Permanent program with at least 100,000 places a year from 2027
evidence.quote: committing to invest over $1.6 billion to 2034-35 to support at least 100,000 Free TAFE and VET places per year from 2027,
The Australian Government has made Free TAFE a permanent feature of the national VET system,
Access to Free TAFE places will be prioritised for target cohorts
Free TAFE will be delivered in partnership with states and territories.

name: VET Student Loans
provider: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations
summary: A Commonwealth loan that pays tuition for approved diploma, advanced diploma and some graduate VET courses, repaid through the tax system.
key: 2026 maximum loan caps: Band 1 $6,428, Band 2 $12,858, Band 3 $19,290, and $96,467 for specific (Schedule 2) courses.
who: Only available for approved courses at diploma, advanced diploma, graduate certificate and graduate diploma level listed in the VET Student Loans (Courses and Loan Caps) Determination 2016.
Your provider must assess you as academically suited to the course.
Citizenship and residency requirements apply.
how: Complete the Request for a VET Student Loan (eCAF) on or before the first census day you want the loan to cover.
catches: You can't borrow more than the loan cap for your course.
VET Student Loans count toward your overall HELP loan limit ($129,883 for most students in 2026).
You repay the debt through the tax system once your income passes the repayment threshold.
The department's 2024 information booklet says full-fee-paying students incur a 20 per cent loan fee and state-subsidised students don't. Check with your provider whether this still applies.

source.label: DEWR: News for VSL providers (2026 loan caps)

evidence.quote: Band 1 (Part 1, Schedule 1) – $6,428
Band 2 (Part 2, Schedule 1) – $12,858
Band 3 (Part 3, Schedule 1) – $19,290
Specific (Schedule 2) – $96,467

evidence.claim: Caps apply from census days in 2026
evidence.quote: These will apply to all units of study (new and continuing VSL students) with a census day of 1 January 2026 or later.
VET Student Loans are only available for approved courses at the diploma, advanced diploma
You must have been assessed by your course provider as academically suited to undertake the course
You must submit the eCAF on or before the first census day for which you would like the loan to apply.
Full fee paying/fee for service students will incur a 20 per cent loan fee on their VET Student Loan.
All FEE-HELP, VET FEE-HELP, VET Students Loans

name: Tuition Protection for VET Student Loans
summary: If your VET Student Loans provider closes or stops your course, the TPS helps you move to a replacement course or re-credits your loan.
who: Students with a VET Student Loan whose provider defaults, for example by closing, not starting a course or stopping it partway through.
how: Contact the Tuition Protection Service on 1300 131 798.
catches: If no suitable replacement course is available, you get a loan re-credit only for the part of the course you paid for but weren't taught.
A replacement provider may charge for some parts of the course, so ask what you'll need to pay.

source.label: Department of Education: VET Student Loans students (TPS)

evidence.quote: the TPS can either help you continue your studies in a suitable replacement course
you are entitled to a loan re-credit on the portion of your course which has been paid for but not delivered.
If you have a VET Student Loan and your provider defaults
within Australia 1300 131 798

name: VET Student Loans Ombudsman
summary: A free, independent complaints service for students with a VET Student Loan or VET FEE-HELP debt who have a problem with their provider.
who: Students who have a VET FEE-HELP or VET Student Loan debt.
The complaint must be about the debt, for example a wrong loan amount, charges after you stopped participating, misleading information or a cancelled enrolment.
how: Complain to your education provider first.
Then use the Ombudsman's online complaint form, or complain by phone, in person or in writing.
catches: Category is the closest fit: this is a complaints service about VET loan debts.

source.label: Commonwealth Ombudsman: VET student loan complaints

evidence.quote: a free, independent and impartial service for students to resolve complaints
We can look into complaints from students who have a VET FEE-HELP or VET Student Loan debt
should lodge a complaint with them first

name: VET Student Loans re-credit for special circumstances
provider: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations
summary: If circumstances beyond your control stopped you finishing VET units, you can ask your provider to re-credit the VET Student Loan for them.
who: VET Student Loans students whose studies were stopped by circumstances beyond their control that began or got worse after the census day.
how: Apply in writing to your provider, with its application form and supporting evidence, within 12 months of the census day for the units.
catches: Your provider can extend the 12-month limit if you show you couldn't apply in time.
If you disagree with the decision, ask the provider for an internal review, then apply to the Administrative Review Tribunal.

source.label: DEWR: VSL student manual, 24. Special circumstances

evidence.claim: Time limit and who to apply to
evidence.quote: you must apply in writing to your provider within 12 months of the census day for the unit/s.
Circumstances are special circumstances if they are:
beyond your control

name: National Training Complaints Hotline
provider: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations
summary: A national phone line and form for complaints about your training experience in VET, referred to the right authority.
who: Anyone with a complaint about their experience while doing vocational training.
how: Call 13 38 73 or complete the online complaints form.
catches: The hotline refers your complaint to the authority best placed to handle it. It doesn't decide it itself.
Category is the closest fit: this is a complaints service.

evidence.quote: the National Training Complaints Hotline can refer your complaint to the most appropriate authority
a complaint relating to your experiences whilst undertaking training

name: Skills for Education and Employment (SEE) Program
provider: Department of Employment and Workplace Relations
summary: Free training in reading, writing, maths, English and basic computer skills for people aged 15 and over who have left school.
who: Australian citizens, permanent visa holders, or people who meet other visa conditions.
Aged 15 years and over and left school.
Need help with reading, writing, maths, English language or digital skills.
how: Contact your local SEE provider, call the National Customer Service Line on 1800 805 260, or ask your employment services provider or Centrelink.

source.label: DEWR: Skills for Education and Employment

evidence.quote: SEE is free!
The Skills for Education and Employment (SEE) Program offers free training
aged 15 years and over and left school

name: Adult Migrant English Program (AMEP)
provider: Department of Home Affairs (via Services Australia)
summary: Free English classes for eligible migrants who speak little or no English, run by providers including many TAFEs.
who: Aged 18 or over and speak little or no English.
Permanent residents, holders of an eligible temporary visa, and some citizens who held an eligible visa before.
People aged 15 to 17 may be able to do AMEP, even if they go to school.
how: Find an AMEP provider on the Department of Home Affairs website and register with them.
catches: If you arrived after 1 October 2020 and are 18 or older, you must register with an AMEP provider within 6 months.
If you have children under school age, you may get free child care while you attend face-to-face classes.

source.label: Services Australia: Adult Migrant English Program

evidence.quote: This is a free course.
If you are 18 or over, you can do AMEP if you speak little or no English.
If you have children under school age, you may get free child care while you attend face to face classes.

name: headspace Work & Study
provider: headspace (funded by the Department of Social Services)
summary: Free career, study and job-application support for young people aged 15 to 25, by webchat, video or phone.
key: A free service for young people aged 15 to 25.
who: Young people aged 15 to 25 anywhere in Australia.
how: Register online and book a time with a specialist, or call 1800 810 794.
catches: Support covers career direction, planning study and course selection, and writing resumes and cover letters.

evidence.quote: A free service for young people aged 15 to 25.
Access support from anywhere in Australia, via webchat, video or phone.
headspace Work & Study is funded by the Australian Government Department of Social Services.

No assets test.
Meet residence rules.

name: Free USI VET transcript
summary: A free, government-authenticated record of all your nationally recognised training since 2015, from your USI account.
key: It's accessible through your USI account, it's government authenticated and it's free.
who: Anyone with a Unique Student Identifier (USI) who has done nationally recognised training.
how: Log in to your USI account through the Student Portal and select View VET Transcript.
